system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID / issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with recovery only for amounts above the basket. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter to playbook thresholds.** Seller’s thresholds screen out too many claims and make the basket a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes limitations apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | 24 months for general claims; keep separate regimes outside that period where required. | **Reject; seek 24 months.** The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s written approval, not given, and should not override other claim regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; establish the separate regime.** Title and capacity exposure must not be reduced to general-warranty limits. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims. | Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent; this is non-waivable. | **Reject; require the carve-out throughout.** The Seller’s all-Claims language could improperly restrict remedies for deliberate wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject general disclosure; retain only specific fair disclosure.** The broad deeming language is not sufficiently targeted to identify matters fairly. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from data-room or public records. | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; if any qualifier remains, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket bar.** Constructive or adviser knowledge should not silently defeat the negotiated warranties and indemnities. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Make it a Completion condition with evidence of satisfaction.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, and consent-on-delivery does not establish compliance with its conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure says not repaid and no final discharge included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require payoff and releases at Completion; do not accept a later release absent the specified approval and undertaking.** The facility remains outstanding and security is not discharged. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are not separately itemised in the funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. | DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **Resolve and document the funding and on-costs explicitly.** The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and are omitted from the draft funds flow. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 ties transfer to cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010’s AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently established either way. | **Broaden the indemnity and retain an effective cure through cleared payment and confirmed transfer.** Payment status and assignment are unverified, and the existing indemnity is too narrow. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no established access, scope or notification duty, and no loss amount. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume neither a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty nor numeric demand. | **Require preservation, investigation and ongoing updates without asserting an unconfirmed outcome.** DD-006 leaves access, scope and legal consequences unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, avoidability, termination and accrual; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess under the agreed price mechanics; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosures do not establish whether renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Limitations and remedies apply to all Claims; Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the global override and leave Tax/IP terms open.** The playbook requires distinct treatment, not assumptions that unresolved categories fall under general terms. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100% of issued shares. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification and supporting evidence.** The register identifies the Seller’s source but does not independently establish clean title or authority. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms **open**; assume neither unlimited liability nor a resolution. | **Do not accept them as settled; negotiate and document the terms separately.** The playbook records no resolution and does not authorise unlimited liability. |
=== END ADVICE ===
